metadata.title: Common Shade — Bangladesh heat resilience snapshot
metadata.no_endorsement: Listing establishes neither partnership nor endorsement. Actors are not ranked.
metadata.published_facts_vs_interpretation: Evidence records describe sources; could_contribute, entry_point, taxonomy and loop links are researcher interpretations/proposals.

evidence_labels.concept: Designed, not yet tried by intended users
evidence_labels.reported: Described by programme team or news, not independently evaluated
evidence_labels.measured: Study, survey or analysis measured it

metadata.review_design: Targeted multilingual primary-source landscape; selected source sections, not full systematic review or full reading of all documents.
metadata.missing_data: null means not verified/not available, never zero.
metadata.institution_mapping_note: Institution tags are functional website mappings, not a claim about legal mandate; university and international research bodies use the nearest health or international-body category.

country.name: Bangladesh
country.scope: Eight documented heat-concern city cases, not nationally ranked most-exposed cities. Targeted primary-source review, not exhaustive systematic review.

city_selection.method: Triangulate original station heatwave analysis, humid/night reanalysis, local assessments and documented action. No harmonised national ranking verified.

heat_context.known: Western/southwestern daytime hotspots coexist with humid urban and night exposure.
heat_context.inferred: Combine work, housing and overnight recovery with warning-to-action design.
heat_context.uncertain: Comparable ward-level exposure, health burden and nationally representative indoor monitoring.

plans_and_law.legal_character: Cross-sector strategic framework; publication page verified, full annexes not reviewed
Government adoption reported by UNFPA; strategic health adaptation plan includes heat. Not a dedicated whole-of-government heat HAP or statutory cash entitlement.
Official clinical/preparedness guidance; implementation not assumed
Plan records municipal approval; national law and actual programme delivery are separate
Pre-2015 legal foundation/background, current portal text checked. Full 2026 amendment audit outstanding.
Pre-2015 foundational/background legal copy explicitly includes heat wave in section 2(11)(a); no automatic fund access inferred
Primary gazette facsimile on mirror; technical energy/sustainability code. Scope, enforcement and amendments to verify.
Existing plan; later draft to 2035 cannot fairly be treated as approved replacement

warnings.proposed_last_mile_channels: NCC plan proposes local media, SMS, loudspeakers, ward offices, religious/educational institutions and visits. Not verified as comprehensive operating coverage.
warnings.note: Meteorological warning, health action and financial payout triggers are separately authorised and validated. No universal WBGT/fan threshold supplied.

occupational_rules.verified_foundation: Ventilation, suitable workplace temperature and drinking-water provisions.
occupational_rules.reason_for_null: Not verified after full 2026 amendment/rules review, not a claim no protection exists.
occupational_rules.equity: Formal-establishment provisions cannot be assumed to reach all informal, migrant, domestic or self-employed workers.

cooling.approach: Proposed passive-first assessment with adequate active cooling where needed; select by humidity, building, task and power.
cooling.cooling_trap: Loop cooling: poorly specified mechanical cooling can add peak demand and waste heat; refrigerant management and affordability would ideally accompany access.

entry_points.proposal: Consent-based city implementation tracker: action, authorised trigger, owner, payer, released funds, access, uptime and feedback
Worker-led work-to-home package: environmental cooling, paid rest, affordable electricity, secure housing permissions and night recovery
Warning-to-cash delivery learning with existing anticipatory-action actors; test exclusion and grievance routes before scale
Align clinic preparedness and heat reporting with HNAP owners, with disaggregated records and evaluated implementation

country.known: Multiple distinct approved frameworks, primary heat research and real anticipatory funding/test mechanisms exist.
country.inferred: Common Shade can support shared delivery/accountability infrastructure with locally accepted governance.
country.uncertain: Current city spending, legal details after amendments, service reach, unit lifecycle costs and causal protection outcomes.

evidence.text: Regional hub with CEEW and BRAC JPGSPH among named partners.

cost.note: No verified intervention unit costs in this record; null does not mean zero.

programmes.limits: Network, not an identified pooled grant allocator. Full Bangladesh country brief inaccessible; public contribution route to confirm.

sources.title: Are hotspots and frequencies of heat waves changing over time?
sources.review_note: Original study; selected methods/results reviewed. BMD daily maximum temperature, 32 stations, 1991–2021. Metric-specific hotspots, not a comprehensive city risk ranking. Some textual/date/count inconsistencies; numerical hotspot ranks not reproduced.

sources.title: Diurnal asymmetry in heat stress intensification across Bangladesh, 1985–2024
sources.review_note: Original analytical study; selected methods, validation and findings reviewed. ERA5-HEAT UTCI at 194 grid points, 0.25 degrees, 1985–2024. Reanalysis-derived/modelled exposure, not measured indoor conditions or clinical outcomes.

sources.title: BMD May 2025 climate summary
sources.review_note: One-page image PDF visually inspected. Temperature observations distinguish station extremes from city population exposure. Text contains an April/May date inconsistency; heatwave-duration counts not reused.

sources.title: Bangladesh Meteorological Department heat-wave warning portal
sources.review_note: Official warning category/portal accessible. This is not verification of a current live alert, local trigger validation, warning receipt or last-mile coverage.

sources.title: Bangladesh faces health and economic risks from rising temperature — report release
sources.review_note: Original publisher summary of An Unsustainable Life. Two-round 2024 household survey of more than 16,000 people and historical climate analysis. Full report methods not fully appraised here; health associations and economic estimates kept separate.

sources.title: Heat Action Plan, Narayanganj City Corporation
sources.review_note: Selected sections of 139-page municipal plan reviewed. PDF page 2 records approval by NCC Administrator on 22 September 2025. Action tables, indicative costs, potential funders and M&E targets are not proof of funding release, appointments or achieved outcomes.

sources.title: Advancing Narayanganj HAP under CLARE
sources.review_note: Programme partner account identifies NCC–ICLEI technical collaboration and CLARE Research for Impact Opportunities Fund supported by FCDO and IDRC. Pre-adoption workshop, not final approval evidence.

sources.title: National Guideline on Heat-Related Illness
sources.review_note: Government/UNICEF clinical and preparedness guideline, primary document mirrored by GHHIN; selected sections reviewed. Guidance is not evidence that all facilities deliver services or treatment is universally free.

sources.title: Guidelines launched to protect children and pregnant women from heat stress
sources.review_note: UNICEF primary launch account establishes DGHS collaboration and B.E.A.T. communication framework. Planned dissemination not verified reach or impact.

sources.title: National Adaptation Plan of Bangladesh 2023–2050
sources.review_note: Official partner publication page reviewed; large full PDF not retrieved through UNFCCC. Cross-sector framework context only; no financing entitlement or detailed operative provision inferred.

sources.title: Bangladesh Labour Act section 52 — ventilation and temperature
sources.publication_date: 2006 original law; current portal text checked
sources.review_note: Primary Bengali section reviewed. Ventilation and suitable-temperature provisions. Pre-2015 legal foundation/background; current application and 2026 amendments require local legal confirmation.

sources.title: Bangladesh Labour Act section 58 — drinking water
sources.publication_date: 2006 original law; current portal text checked
sources.review_note: Primary Bengali section reviewed; cooled summer drinking water provision for establishments ordinarily employing 250 or more workers. Pre-2015 legal foundation/background, not a complete current occupational heat standard.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Employment legislative information
sources.review_note: Official listing and linked amendment detail page opened. Full 2026 amendment schedule not appraised. Therefore no definitive claim of absent numerical WBGT rules, paid-rest entitlement or complete current scope.

sources.title: Disaster Management Act 2012
sources.review_note: Primary legal text mirrored by IFRC; selected definitions and disaster-management provisions reviewed. Section 2(11)(a) explicitly includes heat wave. Pre-2015 foundational/background text; current amendments and budget-release authorisations not audited.

sources.title: Bangladesh National Building Code 2020, Part 3 Chapter 4
sources.review_note: Primary gazette facsimile on nongovernment mirror; chapter on energy efficiency/sustainability reviewed. Covers envelope, windows, shading, roof insulation and systems. Official gazette download timed out; application, amendments and local enforcement need checking.

sources.title: Bangladesh National Cooling Plan for implementation of Montreal Protocol
sources.review_note: Primary Department of Environment/Ozone Cell plan; selected introductory and policy sections reviewed. Existing 2021 plan distinct from later draft-to-2035 listing; no universal appliance eligibility or funded household scheme inferred.

sources.title: Ministry listing — draft National Cooling Plan up to 2035
sources.review_note: Official listing explicitly describes a draft for comment. Not used as proof of approved replacement policy or binding standards.

sources.title: UNEP Ozone Secretariat country profile — Bangladesh
sources.review_note: Treaty profile reviewed: Kigali ratification 8 June 2020 and Montreal Protocol/Multilateral Fund project mechanisms. Restricted refrigerant compliance funding, not general heat adaptation grant eligibility.

sources.title: When social protection anticipates risk — Rajshahi SRSP simulation
sources.review_note: Primary implementer advocacy brief, selected implementation and findings sections reviewed. August 2025 Ward 4 cash simulation reached 301 Old Age Allowance recipients with BDT 2,400 each. Operational test, not independent causal outcome evaluation or permanent nationwide benefit.

sources.title: Start Fund Bangladesh B060 anticipation of heatwave
sources.review_note: Primary allocation record: Jessore and Rajshahi, Start Fund Committee allocation, selected CNRS and ESDO projects. Historical allocation, not open funding or measured project effect.

sources.title: Six Seasons, Four Summers: how to solve fashion’s high heat problem
sources.review_note: Original report selected methods, home exposure, engineering and Table 16 costs reviewed; publisher summary also opened. Eight Dhaka-region factories and 36 worker homes. Exposure measured; cooling reductions, financial returns and home package costs are estimates/modelled, not evaluated retrofit results. Source FX not disclosed.

sources.title: No escaping the heat: informal workers in urban Bangladesh
sources.review_note: Original report selected methods, author/partner details and findings reviewed. Survey of 175 Dhaka informal-worker households plus qualitative work by OKUP. Survey/self-report and extrapolated national costs distinguished; no clinical confirmation of all conditions assumed.

sources.title: Strengthening heat governance in Khulna
sources.review_note: Official resource summary only. Underlying download returned 403; detailed methods/results not appraised. Policy recommendations do not establish adopted city HAP.

sources.title: Impacts of the 2024 heatwave on marginalised groups in Khulna
sources.review_note: Official resource summary only; full PDF inaccessible. No numerical impact estimate reused or independent evaluation claimed.

sources.title: Extreme heat is not just a climate problem — Khulna
sources.review_note: Primary practitioner account; distinguishes Khulna city and rural district experiences. Supports ongoing heat-governance/plan work and Zurich Climate Resilience Alliance relationship, not adopted final KCC HAP or evaluated impact.

sources.title: Heat-Health Adaptation Plan for Bangladesh workshop
sources.review_note: BRAC JPGSPH primary event account identifies LGD/IUPHPSP/World Bank participation and heat-risk research. Workshop and proposals, not national plan approval.

sources.title: Locally Led Adaptation Framework dissemination
sources.review_note: Official partner account: framework approved May 2025, dissemination February 2026; MoEFCC with UNDP, ADB, FCDO, World Bank. General adaptation governance; heat linkage is analytical inference, not specific grant allocation.

sources.title: Creating cooler buildings in Dhaka — Cool to be Cool
sources.review_note: Primary project-team account hosted by challenge organiser. BRAC University/BRAC Urban Development Programme community roof pilot; trust/consent concerns reported. Target coverage not treated as achieved; historical challenge not current call.

sources.title: When heat drains growth — World Bank project-team account
sources.review_note: Primary institutional account says government/Bank heat-health action plan pilots through Urban Health, Nutrition and Population Project. Full project financing/disbursement documents not reviewed here; no grant eligibility inferred.

sources.title: GHHIN South Asia Hub country assessments launch
sources.review_note: Primary network announcement identifies CEEW, BRAC JPGSPH and regional partners, calls for dedicated national/subnational heat plans and surveillance. Bangladesh full report link timed out; announcement not a complete legal or operational audit.

sources.title: UNFPA welcomes adoption of Health National Adaptation Plan
sources.review_note: Official UNFPA account verifies government adoption and launch of HNAP 2026–2031, with MoHFW, WHO, IEDCR and CCHPU; UK/Sweden support. Health adaptation plan includes heat, distinct from dedicated whole-of-government HAP.

sources.title: Bangladesh Health National Adaptation Plan 2026
sources.review_note: Government-hosted full PDF; selected foreword, objectives, Component 4, implementation and budget sections reviewed. IEDCR-led integrated surveillance/early warning and disaggregation are planned directions. Cost estimates and indicator targets not released funding or operating national heat surveillance.
